headline: USS Theodore Roosevelt will not reach CENTCOM before mid-November
dek: The USS Theodore Roosevelt strike group, spotted in the South China Sea south of the Spratly Islands on Wednesday (Al Jazeera satellite imagery), will not enter CENTCOM's area of responsibility before mid-November. Axios, citing a US official, reports the carrier begins a port call in Singapore on…
sources: Axios, citing a US official; satellite imagery analysed by Al Jazeera
fault_line: Is the third carrier a strike clock or a bluff — does 'not before mid-November' mean no big strike until then, or is the threat meant to force the deal now?

sections.what_happened: The USS Theodore Roosevelt strike group, spotted in the South China Sea south of the Spratly Islands on Wednesday (Al Jazeera satellite imagery), will not enter CENTCOM's area of responsibility before mid-November. Axios, citing a US official, reports the carrier begins a port call in Singapore on Friday Nov 6 and stays several days. It would become the third US carrier in the region, joining USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington. Fox News previously reported the strike group plus the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit (~10,000 personnel combined) were expected to arrive by the end of November.
sections.what_verified: Axios (T2) is the origin for the mid-November date and the Singapore port call, via a named-role US official. Al Jazeera (T2) independently corroborates the MOVEMENT via satellite imagery (carrier south of Spratlys, Wednesday, advancing toward the Middle East) — a different sub-claim from the date. Times Now liveblog and the YouTube 'Breaking News Nov 5 Part 2' summary are relays of Axios (Times Now has no declared tier — not counted). NOTE: the mid-November DATE itself rests on Axios alone; the two-family count covers movement + date, not two independent confirmations of the date.
sections.what_disputed: Earlier US official guidance (AP Oct 28; Times Now Oct 31) said end of November — the mid-November figure tightens the CENTCOM-entry date, it does not contradict it. CENTCOM has not officially confirmed the timeline. One of the two carriers now in theatre may rotate out, so a three-carrier posture is not guaranteed. The deployment was announced in October and its composition was already recorded (1100-05, Nov 2); only the TIMELINE is new here.
sections.why_matters: Carrier Math: the third carrier can't reach the Gulf before mid-November — Trump's 'you'll know soon enough' runs into a hardware clock. Counted numbers: 3rd carrier, ~10,000 personnel, mid-November.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Axios report Nov 5; Times Now liveblog entry 02:35 IST = 01:05 Nov 6; YouTube summary) -- USS Theodore Roosevelt will not reach CENTCOM before mid-November; Singapore port call from Friday

totw_analysis: Our read: Carrier Math: the third carrier can't reach the Gulf before mid-November — Trump's 'you'll know soon enough' runs into a hardware clock. Counted numbers: 3rd carrier, ~10,000 personnel, mid-November. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the third carrier a strike clock or a bluff — does 'not before mid-November' mean no big strike until then, or is the threat meant to force the deal now?
